name: Cialis / tadalafil for blood flow

lead: Tadalafil, sold as Cialis, is a prescription phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitor approved for erectile dysfunction, benign prostatic hyperplasia and pulmonary arterial hypertension. By raising cGMP it relaxes smooth muscle in blood vessels, which increases local blood flow.

Looksmaxxing forum users discuss low, regular amounts for circulation, 'pumps' and vascularity during training, and for erection quality. Clinical trials have measured erectile function, urinary symptoms and lung-artery pressure; none has tested veins, pumps or appearance in healthy lifters.

paras: Forum reports describe generic tadalafil tablets taken by mouth on an ongoing schedule, sometimes alongside testosterone or other compounds, with users logging effects over a couple of weeks (for example more stamina and warmth). Because tadalafil acts for about a day and a half, forum users discuss every-day and every-other-day patterns. Non-prescription sourcing and dosing are discussed in threads but are not endorsed here.

Common side effects are headache, flushing, indigestion, back or muscle pain and nasal congestion. Rare serious events include priapism, sudden vision loss and sudden hearing loss, and it must not be combined with nitrate medicines because of a risk of a severe drop in blood pressure. It is prescription-only in the US, UK, EU and Australia, and a clinician can review heart health and other medicines first.

angle.text: Users take tadalafil in the hope of better circulation: fuller training pumps, more visible veins and stronger erections. The vessel-relaxing mechanism is established in clinical pharmacology; the appearance payoff rests on user reports.

lead: Tadalafil, best known by the brand name Cialis, is a selective PDE5 inhibitor developed by ICOS and Eli Lilly and approved by the US FDA for erectile dysfunction in 2003 [1]. It is also approved for benign prostatic hyperplasia (2011) and, as Adcirca, for pulmonary arterial hypertension (2009) [1]. Its long duration of action, up to about 36 hours, earned it the nickname 'the weekend pill' [1].

In looksmaxxing and gym communities, tadalafil is discussed as a blood-flow compound: users post updates describing improved erection quality, stamina, and the hope of a better pump and a more vascular look during training [2][3][4]. The route is oral tablets, and the posts often pair it with other compounds such as testosterone or the growth hormone secretagogue MK-677 [5].

Published research on tadalafil covers erectile function, lower urinary tract symptoms and pulmonary arterial hypertension [6][7][8]. Its vessel-relaxing mechanism is well described in pharmacology, and a small amount of exercise-related work exists, but no trial has studied it for muscle pump, vein visibility or other appearance outcomes in healthy lifters [4][9]. Health professionals in several countries have commented on its growing use in gyms by men without erectile dysfunction [10].
infobox: About 17.5 hours; effect up to 36 hours [1]
Glaxo / ICOS, then ICOS and Eli Lilly (Lilly ICOS)

paras: Tadalafil is approved for erectile dysfunction, urinary symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where it dilates pulmonary vessels and lowers pressure [1][6][7]. In BPH it has performed similarly to tamsulosin in studies, and Peyronie's disease is under study [1]. Guideline reviews of lower urinary tract symptoms in men list PDE5 inhibitors among treatment options [8].

In PAH, tadalafil is used alone or in combination. A 16-week placebo-controlled trial of 405 patients tested it as monotherapy or added to bosentan, and later trials examined it in combination with ambrisentan or macitentan [7][11][12].

Forum members describe tadalafil as a way to improve circulation, training 'pumps', stamina, mood and erections. One user's multi-week log reports increased stamina after the second week and notes that the effect seemed to persist with wider spacing between tablets [2]. Another thread logs a first-time user's warmth, mild headache and a slight, short-lived engorgement without stimulation [3]. A separate thread discusses combining tadalafil with MK-677 [5], and others ask about combining it with testosterone or hCG or list it among a set of purchases for appearance-related projects [9][13].

Users discuss several patterns because of the long half-life: ongoing small daily amounts, or every-other-day schedules. The wiki does not give dosing guidance. A thread asking whether tadalafil 'potentially helps with depression mood' shows the mood claim circulating alongside the circulation claim [14].

Commentary from fitness retailers and media describes the same idea: a PDE5 inhibitor may increase blood flow to working muscle and strengthen the 'pump', and some men report better vascularity and endurance [4]. The same retailer article states that tadalafil is not an anabolic agent and that evidence for strength or growth gains in healthy lifters is limited, and notes that it is published by a company that sells supplements [4].

In 2025 a Brazilian pharmacy council news item described a gym trend, called 'Cialis do treino' (workout Cialis), among men under 30 without erectile dysfunction, fuelled by social media and easy access. Health professionals quoted there said there is no proof it contributes to muscle development and warned of heart-rate, fainting and blood-pressure risks, especially with stimulants [10].

Glaxo and ICOS began a partnership in August 1991, and under it the compound later known as tadalafil was discovered; ICOS studied it as IC351 from 1993 and received a patent in 1994, the year Pfizer researchers noticed sildenafil's erectile effects in a heart-drug trial [1]. Phase 1 trials began in 1995 and phase 2 trials for erectile dysfunction in 1997. In 1998 ICOS and Eli Lilly formed Lilly ICOS, LLC, which filed its new drug application in 2002 and reported that the drug worked for up to 36 hours [1].

The FDA approved Cialis in 2003 [1]. Advertising during the 2004 Super Bowl led the FDA to require more side effects, including priapism, to be listed, and in 2006 ads were limited to audiences that were over 90 percent adult [1]. Eli Lilly bought ICOS for 2.3 billion US dollars in 2007 [1]. The PAH formulation Adcirca was approved in the US in 2009 after Lilly sold US PAH rights to United Therapeutics in 2008, and the BPH indication followed in October 2011 [1]. A generic became available in the UK in 2017 [1].

Sexual stimulation releases nitric oxide, which raises cGMP and relaxes smooth muscle; tadalafil blocks PDE5, the enzyme that breaks cGMP down, so it has little effect without stimulation [1]. A review of nitric oxide synthases notes that PDE5 inhibitors require at least some residual nitric oxide synthase activity to act [15]. Compared with sildenafil and vardenafil, tadalafil inhibits PDE6 and PDE1 less and PDE11 more [1].

Proponents in gym communities extend this vessel-relaxing action to skeletal muscle blood flow, the basis of the 'pump' idea; fitness commentary calls this biologically plausible but not proven for lifters [4].

Onset is about 30 minutes. Tadalafil has a half-life of about 17.5 hours and acts for up to 36 hours, compared with roughly four to five hours for sildenafil and vardenafil [1]. It is about 94 percent protein bound, metabolised mainly by the liver enzyme CYP3A4, and excreted in feces and urine [1]. The long half-life supports once-daily regimens in PAH and BPH [1].

The most commonly reported side effects in trials were headache and dyspepsia, generally mild to moderate and less frequent with continued use [6]. Other reported effects include back and muscle pain, flushing, nasal congestion, dizziness and fatigue [1]. Priapism, vision loss linked to non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) and sudden hearing loss are rare serious events; the FDA linked the class to NAION in 2005 and required stronger hearing-loss warnings in 2007, and a 2019 meta-analysis reported no association between tadalafil and NAION [1].

Tadalafil is not recommended with nitrate drugs such as nitroglycerin because of a risk of a serious drop in blood pressure, and caution is advised in cardiovascular disease [1]. Commentary on gym use also lists interactions with alpha-blockers, blood-pressure medicines, alcohol and stimulants, and notes that unverified supply carries risks of counterfeit or wrongly dosed products [4].

Tadalafil is prescription-only in the US, UK, EU and Australia (Schedule 4 in Australia), with generics available [1]. Looksmax.org threads include members asking where to obtain it, including one user who says a purchased liquid form tasted poor and whose source he was unsure of [16], and others asking about sourcing in the EU or buying Cialis or Viagra [17]. The wiki does not give sourcing details. Competitive athletes are directed in fitness commentary to check anti-doping rules [4].

A Drugs review of tadalafil trials reported that on-demand 10 or 20 mg doses gave significantly greater improvement than placebo in erectile function scores over 12 weeks, with headache and dyspepsia the most common adverse events and no significant difference in cardiovascular events versus placebo [6].

In pulmonary arterial hypertension, a 16-week double-blind placebo-controlled study of 405 patients evaluated tadalafil alone or with bosentan [7]. The AMBITION trial compared initial combination ambrisentan plus tadalafil with monotherapy [12], and a phase 3 trial of 187 patients found a single-tablet macitentan/tadalafil combination reduced pulmonary vascular resistance by about 29 percent versus macitentan and 28 percent versus tadalafil alone at week 16 [11].

A 2025 JAMA review of lower urinary tract symptoms in men covers PDE5 inhibitors among therapies [8]. A randomized trial in young subfertile men with chronic prostatitis and pelvic pain tested a multi-drug regimen that included tadalafil [18].

No trials have tested tadalafil for vascularity, training pump or other appearance outcomes in healthy people. Fitness commentary notes that chronic tadalafil improved endothelial function in men with elevated cardiovascular risk, that a single dose did not substantially improve anaerobic performance indices, that a phase 3 trial in boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy did not slow decline, and that a small study in non-obese men with mild erectile dysfunction linked daily tadalafil to higher lean mass; the author stresses that none was a lifting or hypertrophy trial [4].

In 2026 an NPR report on online clinics and influencers promoting Cialis as a longevity drug drew a Hacker News discussion of the idea [19]. Commenters raised the possibility of selection bias (men who seek erectile treatment may be healthier), the blood-pressure-lowering effect, and cautions about hearing and eyesight, and a second thread asked how the drug compares with established medicine [19][19]. This longevity framing is separate from the looksmaxxing blood-flow use.
